verdict.rationale: Restate documents that handlers can be invoked over HTTP, through typed clients, or from Kafka topics. Any handler can act as a durable webhook endpoint with exactly-once processing and idempotency-key deduplication. Fan-out is documented only as an in-code pattern (dispatching work to multiple agents and combining results), not as one event routed to many subscribed functions, and declarative trigger configuration is not shown. Missing for 10: declarative trigger/subscription configuration, documented one-event-to-many-functions fan-out at the trigger level, independent corroboration of the Kafka/webhook triggers.

support.subject: As a backend developer, events from my app, webhooks, or queues trigger workflows declaratively, and one event can fan out to many functions

citations.quote: There are three ways to invoke a handler: over HTTP, using typed clients, or through Kafka topics.
Any handler can be a durable webhook endpoint. No need to do anything special or extra!
Restate persists all incoming events, and ensures that they are processed exactly once, across failures and restarts... Let Restate deduplicate events on an idempotency key.
Restate eliminates this complexity by providing **lightweight, transactional event processing** with zero consumer management and built-in state.
Fan out work to multiple agents, then combine the results.
